account:
Today I have kept my ordinary appointments: office business, the mill inspection, lunch at home, council correspondence, and tea with my dockside neighbour. I have now returned to town hall for the sixteen-thirty office appointment. The secretary reported no new council letters. Freight has proposed lighting both ferry landings and marking waiting areas away from the water; I requested a cost estimate, not approval of the work.

The unusual business is an organised civic presentation in the great hall from eighteen to eighteen thirty. The appointment supplement describes it as appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople, which I approved yesterday. The organisers specifically asked me not to arrive early because they need time to finish arrangements around their work. The innkeeper is to meet me shortly beforehand and escort me in at eighteen exactly; the secretary has confirmed this. The innkeeper is already waiting near the hall this afternoon.

There are signs of coordination among the tradespeople. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern, though I do not know their purpose. Today the innkeeper told the baker that an outstanding bread delivery had arrived and no additional order was needed. My neighbour also mentioned that delivery. These supplies might relate to the presentation, perhaps refreshments and preparations, but I have not seen that connection established.

I have felt that something was going on without me. A planned appreciation gathering, possibly with a surprise element, is my best explanation for the timing restrictions and coordination, rather than any confirmed secret municipal project. There has also been vague bridge-or-port talk, but neither the innkeeper nor my neighbour has supplied definite information; my neighbour has noticed nothing unusual at the docks. I should not confuse that rumour with freight's concrete ferry-lighting proposal or treat it as evidence of an actual bridge or port change.
